test_header_comment: Native NB2 coordinate-spatial slope-only SD regression:
spatial(0 + x | site, coords = coords)  with  sd(site, level = "spatial") ~ z
Model: eta_i = X_i beta + x_i * tau_g[i] * u_g[i], u ~ N(0, Sigma),
tau_g = exp(alpha0 + alpha1 * z_g), NB2 variance mu + sigma^2 mu^2.
Template: test-poisson-spatial-sd-regression.R (slope-only arm) and
test-nbinom2-relmat-spatial-intercept-sd-regression.R (NB2 oracle).
Oracles used here:
* a dense Laplace approximation of the marginal likelihood at the fitted
parameters (the native engine is a Laplace fit, so they agree to
optimiser precision), with per-observation weight w_i = x_i;
* constant-SD equivalence: `sd(...) ~ 1` must reproduce the scalar
`spatial(0 + x | site)` fit (log-likelihood, mu coefficients, and
exp(intercept) = scalar SD);
* nesting: the `~ z` model contains the `~ 1` model, so its maximised
log-likelihood cannot be lower;
* exact link algebra: predict() = exp(X alpha) at each site.
Disclosure: the dense-Laplace oracle and the data-generating covariance are
built with drmTMB:::drm_spatial_coords_precision (the helper under test). The
helper's name alignment is therefore checked separately, against a kernel
rebuilt here from the unshuffled ring (same exponential / median-distance /
1e-6-jitter formula, so the formula itself is mirrored, not independent).
Name alignment: the coordinate rows are passed in a fixed non-symmetric
shuffle of the site-level order (a ring reversed is a symmetry of the kernel
and would hide positional misalignment). The test asserts that reading the
shuffled rows by position changes the precision matrix and the oracle.
Tolerances were fixed before the first run: dense-Laplace match 1e-6
(relative); kernel rebuild 1e-8; positional precision must differ by more
than 0.5 (max abs); positional oracle log-likelihood must differ by more than
1000 x (1e-6 x |logLik|); recovery of the z slope: positive and within 0.6 of
the truth (24 sites).

review_note: Independent review confirmed a base-R dense Laplace oracle for NB2(log) with a slope-only coordinate field (weight w = x, observed information size*mu*(size+y)/(size+mu)^2, size = 1/sigma^2) for the single linked row: native nbinom2 mu, spatial(0+x|site, coords), sd(site, level='spatial') ~ z. Agreement is 1e-6 relative. The covariance is the package spatial helper, so the kernel itself is not an independent definition. The test discloses this and rebuilds the exponential / median-distance / 1e-6 kernel by hand from the unshuffled ring (1e-8 match). This confirms implementation, not the kernel convention. Emulated-bug sensitivity exists: coordinate rows are passed in a shuffled order, reading them by position changes the precision matrix (>0.5) and the oracle by more than 1000x tolerance. Constant-SD equivalence, nesting, prediction identity and the refusal of a within-site z are also tested. Focused test rerun on the current worktree: 23 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped. Manifest rehash: 3 of 10 entries differ (R/drmTMB.R, R/methods.R, src/drmTMB.cpp). They were changed by later lane commits, so the old states could not be reproduced. The current-file rerun is the evidence. Does not establish the mesh_precision provider, se=TRUE inference, calibration, coverage or Julia parity. 24 sites, loose recovery band 0.6. The receipt manifest needs a refresh. Scope note (2026-11-02, after verifier): every linked fit is slope-only; the claim covers the slope-member SD of the unlabelled structured field only. Per mechanism-templates.tsv the unlabelled intercept and slope are independent fields (blockdiag(K, K)), so no companion structured intercept is exercised or claimed.
